critical_bugs.description: MALFORMED OpPhi for conditional coopmat reassignment. detect_loop_carried_coopmat() (body.rs:855-888) scans INTO if/else (stmt_reassigns_binding descends if/else at the current loop level). A coopmat accumulator reassigned inside an `if` WITHOUT break/continue — e.g. `for k { if k>gate { acc = coopmat_mul_add(a,b,acc); } }` — is therefore DETECTED as loop-carried and a header OpPhi is emitted. But after emit_if, var_ids[acc] holds the then-branch SSA id, which is defined only in the then-block and does NOT dominate the continue/latch block. The phi's latch operand (body.rs:1018-1023, captured as var_ids[bid] after body emission) then references a non-dominating id. The break/continue guard (Step 2, body.rs:938-950) does NOT cover this case (no break/continue present). REPRODUCED: compiling such a kernel emits SPIR-V that spirv-val REJECTS: `In OpPhi instruction '%44', ID '%67' definition does not dominate its parent '%42'`. Because emit_module() does NOT run spirv-val internally and the core compile_source_with_meta -> prepare_kernel_checked -> dispatch path does not validate either (only the MCP path validates), this malformed SPIR-V flows to GPU dispatch as UB. No SHIPPED kernel triggers it (all reassign acc unconditionally at loop level), so it is LATENT, but it is exactly the malformed-phi class the review must reject. Fix: either (a) extend the Step-2 guard to reject coopmat accumulators that are NOT reassigned on ALL paths through the loop body (conservative hard error, symmetric to the break/continue reject), or (b) restrict detection to unconditional top-level Assign (do not descend into if/else for the carried-binding scan), so a conditionally-reassigned coopmat is rejected/handled rather than silently producing a non-dominating latch operand.
critical_bugs.line: 747-782 (stmt_reassigns_binding descends if/else) + 938-950 (guard misses conditional partial-reassign) + 1018-1023 (latch capture of non-dominating id)

warnings.description: emit_module() returns SPIR-V words WITHOUT running spirv-val; the core compile_source_with_meta -> prepare_kernel_checked -> dispatch_handle path (used by tests and the public driver API) does not validate before GPU submission (only the MCP compile_variant/bench_variant path calls validate_spirv). This converts the malformed-phi bug above from a clean compile error into latent GPU UB. Even after the phi fix, consider validating in prepare_kernel_checked.

Two .expect() panics in new lib code: body.rs:957 (pre_header value) and body.rs:1021 (latch value). Both are safe by construction today (Step 5 inserts phi_id into var_ids before the body; detection requires var_ids.contains_key), so they cannot fire for well-formed input, but they are panics in library code. Prefer returning BodyCodegenError::UnexpectedHir for defense in depth.

opphi_correctness_check: PARTIAL — correct for unconditional top-level reassignment (predecessors are exactly (pre_header_value,pre_header_label)+(latch_value,continue_label); continue_label IS the physical back-edge predecessor regardless of body control flow; phi post-inserted at InsertPoint::Begin before OpLoopMerge per SPIR-V 2.4; merge block restored after insert via select_block(merge_block_idx); var_ids[B]=phi_id set before body AND restored to phi_id on exit for zero-trip/post-loop correctness). INCORRECT for conditional partial reassignment inside an if (non-dominating latch operand -> spirv-val reject). AT-1701/1702/1703 spirv-val + structural asserts pass; AT-1707 numeric proof passes.
at1707_load_bearing: YES — opphi_coopmat_accumulate.axc loops K_ITER=4 accumulating the SAME tile; the test's CPU reference is an INDEPENDENT cpu_f16_matmul_reference(A,B) multiplied by K_ITER (not a hardcoded constant), and it asserts max_diff == 0.0 (bit-exact). If OpPhi were broken (accumulator reset to coopmat_zero each iteration) the GPU would produce 1*(A.B) while the reference is 4*(A.B) -> max_diff != 0 -> test FAILS. Orchestrator confirms PASS bit-exact on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, so the proof is genuine and load-bearing.

Mutability (!is_mutable -> AssignImmutable) and induction-var rejection precede routing. A scalar assignment cannot route to coopmat and vice versa. body.rs Assign (510-522) routes by coopmat_binding_ids: coopmat -> var_ids.insert (SSA rebind, no store); scalar -> b.store. A coopmat binding can NEVER hit b.store (set populated from BindingTy::CoopMatrix in prelude).

summary: OpPhi loop-carried SSA is correctly emitted and GPU-PROVEN bit-exact (AT-1707 genuinely load-bearing) for the shipped pattern of UNCONDITIONAL top-level coopmat accumulator reassignment; typecheck/Assign routing is sound; scalars are untouched (AT-1700); break/continue over a carried coopmat are safely rejected; the AT-1620/1622 full-coopmat-matmul deferral is HONEST (empty #[ignore] stubs, no wrong-computing numeric assert ships, competitive bench removed, DESIGN/ROADMAP make no false bit-exact/TFLOPS claim). HOWEVER, REQUEST_CHANGES on one reproduced malformed-phi hole: a coopmat accumulator reassigned inside an `if` (no break/continue) is detected as loop-carried but produces an OpPhi whose latch operand does not dominate the continue block — spirv-val rejects it, and because emit_module/compile->dispatch do not validate, it is latent GPU UB. No shipped kernel triggers it, but the brief makes 'any malformed-phi risk' a blocking condition. Fix: extend the Step-2 guard to reject (or correctly handle) coopmat accumulators not reassigned on all loop-body paths, symmetric to the existing break/continue reject. Single most dangerous remaining issue: the conditional-partial-reassignment malformed OpPhi (non-dominating latch operand).
